name: Miguel de Cervantes Saavedra
credit: Portrait attributed to Juan de Jáuregui, c. 1600 · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Miguel de Cervantes Saavedra was born at Alcalá de Henares in 1547 and died in Madrid in 1616. He is the author of Don Quixote (1605, 1615), the founding masterpiece of the modern novel. He was wounded at the battle of Lepanto in 1571, spent five years as a captive in Algiers, and later served the crown as a purveyor and tax collector.

Verse runs through his whole career: sonnets, ballads and occasional poems, the pastoral novel La Galatea, and the long satirical Viaje del Parnaso (1614), in which he reviewed the poets of his day. The archive carries one sonnet to friendship, from The Oxford Book of Spanish Verse (1913); verse set within the novels is not included.

poems.title: Soneto: Santa amistad, que con ligeras alas
poems.author: Miguel de Cervantes Saavedra
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Spanish Verse (1913)
poems.text:
Santa amistad, que con ligeras alas,
tu apariencia quedándose en el suelo,
entre benditas almas, en el cielo
subiste alegre a las impíreas salas;
desde allá, quando quieres, nos señalas
la falsa faz cubierta con tu velo,
por quien a vezes se trasluce el celo
de buenas obras, que a la fin son malas.
Deja el cielo, amistad, o no permitas
que el engaño se vista tu librea,
con que destruye a la intencion sincera;
que si tus apariencias no le quitas,
presto ha de verse el mundo en la pelea
de la discorde confusion primera.
